intro.title: Welcome to Larache — Lixus and the Atlantic
intro.p1: Larache sits on Morocco's northwestern Atlantic coast at the mouth of the Loukkos River. It is quieter than Tangier or Asilah, with a compact medina, Spanish-era streets and one of the region's most important ancient sites: Lixus.
intro.p2: Plan one or two nights for the ruins, a waterfront walk and a slower coastal pace. It combines easily with Asilah or as a stop between Tangier and Rabat.

lixus.title: Lixus archaeological site
lixus.p1: Lixus is Larache's headline stop: a hilltop site with Phoenician roots and major Roman remains, overlooking the Loukkos estuary. It is quieter than Volubilis and easy to combine with a Larache stay.
lixus.p2: Allow time to walk the ruins and the views. Wear sturdy shoes, bring water and check opening hours locally.
lixus.tip: Morning visits are cooler and often less crowded.

medina.title: Medina of Larache
medina.p1: Larache's medina is compact and lived-in — lanes, small shops and a slower rhythm than the big imperial cities.
medina.p2: Go in the morning for softer light. Dress modestly and ask before close-up photos of people.
medina.tip: Pair with a café stop near the waterfront.

waterfront.title: Waterfront & port
waterfront.p1: The Atlantic edge and port area give Larache its coastal character — fishing boats, sea air and an easy evening stroll.
waterfront.p2: Sunset light is often soft along the water. Keep valuables secure in busier spots.
waterfront.tip: Good place for a simple fish plate when the catch is in.

spanish.title: Spanish-era streets
spanish.p1: Larache retains a clear Spanish protectorate imprint: plazas, administrative buildings and a street grid that contrasts with the medina.
spanish.p2: A short walk is enough to sense the dual character of the town — Moroccan medina and colonial-era centre.
spanish.tip: Best combined with the medina the same morning.

beach.title: Beach & dunes
beach.p1: Sandy Atlantic beaches near Larache offer open space and strong coastal light. Conditions depend on wind and swell.
beach.p2: Swim only where it looks safe; Atlantic currents can be strong. Bring sun protection.
beach.tip: Late afternoon is pleasant for a walk when the heat eases.

loukkos.title: Loukkos estuary
loukkos.p1: The Loukkos meets the Atlantic at Larache, creating wetlands and a green corridor that frames Lixus and the coast.
loukkos.p2: Birdlife and open views reward a short outing; respect private land and fragile banks.
loukkos.tip: Pairs naturally with a Lixus visit.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Larache?
q1.answer: One night covers Lixus and the centre; two nights if you want a slower coastal pace and Asilah.

q2.question: What is Lixus?
q2.answer: An important Phoenician and Roman archaeological site on a hill near Larache, overlooking the Loukkos estuary.

q3.question: How do I get to Larache?
q3.answer: By road from Tangier (about 1.5h), Asilah (about 40 min) or Rabat (about 2.5–3h). Grands taxis and buses serve the coast.

q4.question: Is Larache quieter than Asilah?
q4.answer: Yes — Larache is less polished and less crowded, with a stronger everyday port-town feel.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2–3 Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for Lixus, the medina and Atlantic air without rushing.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Head to Lixus while the light is soft. Walk the ruins and take in the Loukkos views.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Explore the compact medina and Spanish-era streets at a slow pace.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Stroll the port edge and eat a simple fish or grill plate.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Atlantic beach walk or Loukkos edge if the wind is calm.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Café time, market browsing and rest before another coastal hop.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Tagine or seafood and an early night.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Coffee and a last look at the waterfront before the road.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Continue to Asilah for ramparts and murals, or Tangier for the kasbah and port.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Overnight in Asilah, Tangier or further along the coast depending on your route.
